title: SSOT adoption sweep: skills, README, and docs cite @-addresses instead of copying item text
description:
Epic 2821e177 made project knowledge addressable (`@/<kind>/<self-id>` over invariants, rules, gates, requirements, definitions), but the surrounding tooling still copies prose: skills paste invariant/rule text into dispatch prompts and review protocols, and README/docs restate registry content. Copied text re-creates the drift problem the epic solved. Sweep the authored surfaces to cite addresses and resolve them on demand, per the principle recorded in `dev/studies/addressing-v2-item-use-cases.md` §3: write the fact once in the registry or issue section that owns it; everywhere else, cite the address.

## Operating rule: three tiers by read heat

Classify every occurrence of registry-owned text (invariant/rule/gate/requirement/definition content) on a swept surface into one tier; the tier decides the edit:

1. **Projection (hot path, loaded every session).** Text machine-rendered from a registry (the CLAUDE.md invariant region, `docs/reference/rules-and-gates.md`) stays inline: it is a renderer-owned copy, safe by construction. Leave it alone, and never hand-cite where a projection already inlines the text.
2. **Gloss + address (warm prose where readability matters).** README, docs narrative, and skill explanations keep a clause-length paraphrase followed by the address: "append an event per state change (`@/invariant/INV-EVENT-LOG`)". The address is authoritative; the gloss is a hint and stays short enough that drift is harmless.
3. **Bare address + resolve (behavioral text agents act on).** Dispatch prompts, review protocols, and gate-semantics passages in lead skills cite the address without paraphrasing behavior. Each dispatch-prompt template carries one standing instruction — cited `@/…` addresses are resolvable context; resolve them via `jit item show` before acting on them (chained calls in one shell invocation resolve several at once) — rather than a per-citation instruction. Lead review protocols verify cited addresses resolve.

Decision rule per occurrence: rendered from a registry -> tier 1, leave as is. An agent will act on the text -> tier 3, replace the paraphrase with the address. Otherwise explanatory -> tier 2, gloss + address. Skill-owned rules (e.g. lead-invariant sections) are the skill's own content, not registry items, and stay as prose.

## Surfaces

1. Repo-tracked skills under `.claude/skills/` (jit-manage, jit-breakdown, jit-parallel, jit-execution-lead, jit-planning-lead, jit-project-lead and their references/): apply the tier rule. Restatements of invariant/rule/gate behavior become tier-3 citations (`@/invariant/INV-EVENT-LOG`, `@/rule/coverage-preview`, `@/gate/code-review`); explanatory mentions become tier-2 gloss + address. Dispatch-prompt templates gain the standing resolve instruction; lead review protocols verify cited addresses resolve.
2. `README.md` and `docs/`: introduce the addressing scheme and `jit item` as the way to cite project knowledge; every place quoting an invariant/rule/gate definition carries its address (tier 2). `docs/reference/rules-and-gates.md` is the rendered SSOT example to point at (tier 1).
3. `CLAUDE.md`: guidance outside the rendered invariant region cites addresses rather than restating rule/gate behavior.
4. Conventions: document the `enforces:@/rule/…` / `enforces:@/gate/…` label convention for work that changes enforcement mechanisms.

## Sequencing

A tier-3 citation must never resolve to less information than the prose it replaces. Rule descriptions (`8d2c5ff3`, a dependency of this issue) enrich `jit item show @/rule/…` and the rendered reference; the skill sweep lands after it so resolved text carries the behavioral detail the removed prose held.

User-global skill copies under `~/.claude/skills/` are outside this repository; this task updates repo-tracked surfaces and notes the sync expectation in the README section it adds.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: every repo-tracked skill file that restates invariant/rule/gate content is converted per the tier rule — behavioral text to bare address (tier 3), explanatory text to clause-length gloss + address (tier 2) — and each dispatch-prompt template carries the standing resolve instruction; a sweep table (file -> tier -> change) is linked to this issue via `jit doc add` as evidence.
- [hard] REQ-02: README and docs/ introduce the addressing scheme and the cite-the-address convention; quoted registry content carries its address; renderer-owned projections stay inline and are identified as such.
- [hard] REQ-03: CLAUDE.md guidance cites addresses for rule/gate/invariant references outside the rendered invariant region.
- [hard] REQ-04: every `@/…` address cited by the swept surfaces resolves via `jit item show` (dangling-citation check attached as evidence); `jit validate` stays green.
